title: Murshid Quli Khan Formally Appointed Nawab
subtitle: Bengal enters a stronger quasi-autonomous nawabi phase under Mughal sanction.
summary: In 1717, Murshid Quli Khan was formally appointed subahdar/nawab of Bengal, marking the institutional start of the nawabi regime. The arrangement preserved Mughal suzerainty while expanding provincial fiscal-political autonomy.
heroTagline: 1717 formalized Bengal's nawabi order within, yet increasingly apart from, the Mughal center.
whyItMatters: This event matters because it explains how Bengal's provincial power became structurally stronger before the 1757 crisis.
longTermLegacy: The 1717 settlement consolidated a provincial regime whose elite alignments, revenue structures, and political vulnerabilities shaped the road to Plassey.
identityMemoryNotes: In Bengal's historical memory, 1717 marks the consolidation of nawabi authority as a distinct regional order before colonial takeover.
